strongest_bounded_proposition: South Arabian/Sabaic epigraphy supports captivity and slave status, including proprietary purchase/sale relations in some first-millennium contexts.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not treat every ʿbd as proof of chattel slavery or infer prevalence from inscription counts.
territorial_practice_summary: Slavery/enslavement is supported in the Sabaic/South Arabian evidence package; prevalence at 500 BCE is unassessed.
external_network_summary: Captivity and movement are evidenced, but trade intensity is not a territorial-prevalence proxy.
terminology_category_qualification: ʿbd can mean servant/subordinate; transactional and captive contexts are more diagnostic.
temporal_scope_precision: First-millennium evidence supports a broad c.500 BCE context, not exact-date continuity.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible packet only; non-English/non-digitized scholarship not exhaustively searched.
